title: 1950 FIFA World Cup
prose:
Staged in Brazil from 24 June to 16 July 1950, this was the first World Cup held after the Second World War, the 1942 and 1946 editions having been cancelled. Thirteen teams contested a tournament of singular design: four group stages fed not into a knockout bracket but into a final four-team round-robin pool, making 1950 the only World Cup ever decided by a round-robin final stage rather than a single championship match. It was also the first edition in which the defending champions were eliminated in the first round, as Italy departed early.

The host nation arrived at the final pool in imperious form, thrashing Sweden 7–1 and Spain 6–1 and seeming destined for the title. Brazil needed only a draw in the decisive match against Uruguay to be crowned. On 16 July, at the newly built Estádio do Maracanã in Rio de Janeiro, an official 173,850 spectators packed in for what remains among the highest attendances for any football match; total tournament attendance exceeded one million.

Brazil duly took the lead through Friça early in the second half, but Uruguay refused to fold. Schiaffino equalised in the 66th minute and Ghiggia struck the winner in the 79th, the match settled 2–1 in regular time with no extra time or penalties. The result, met by stunned silence in the Maracanã, became known as the 'Maracanazo' and endures as one of football's greatest upsets.

Uruguay were champions for the second time, twenty years after their triumph in 1930. Brazil finished as runners-up and Sweden took third place. Brazil's Ademir was the tournament's top scorer with nine goals. No official best-player or Golden Ball award existed for this edition, so no individual was so honoured.
